sections.h2: Which Rockdale County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Three separate bodies touch a Rockdale County tax bill. The Board of Assessors sets the value, the Tax Commissioner collects the money, and the elected governing bodies set the millage rates. The Rockdale tax facts page says the assessors answer to state law, the commissioners control only the assessors' budget, and the Tax Commissioner is an elected office that does not report to the assessors.

  • Board of Assessors: 770-278-7676, P.O. Box 562, Conyers, GA 30012. Confirm the current office location by phone before you visit.
  • Tax Commissioner: 770-278-7600, or text 678-964-4712, at rockdaletaxoffice.org.
  • Millage rates: set by the Board of Education, the Board of Commissioners and, inside city limits, the city council.

sections.h2: What is Rockdale County like for homeowners?
sections.html:
Rockdale covers 129.82 square miles of land and holds 720.8 people per square mile. The 2025 Census estimate is 98,416 residents, up 5.3 percent from the 2020 base, and the tax and assessor offices are in Conyers.

Owners live in 69.6 percent of homes. The median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 is $292,900, median gross rent is $1,525, and median household income is $77,247. Workers average 33.7 minutes getting to work, and 32.4 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher. All figures come from the Census QuickFacts table.

For a seller, the median value of $292,900 and the median rent of $1,525 point to a market where a single unpaid year of tax is a larger balance than in a low-value county. Check the status of the parcel with the Tax Commissioner before you list.

sections.h2: How is a Rockdale County tax bill calculated?
sections.html:
The county assesses property at 40 percent of market value. Exemptions are subtracted to give a taxable value, and the millage rate is applied to that remainder. The tax facts page lists three appraisal methods the assessors use: sales comparison, cost, and income capitalization.

Your bill can change even when the millage rate holds still, because a changed value or a lost exemption moves the result. The same page says the assessors' goal is fair market value, and the state tests each county's digest for accuracy.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Rockdale County value?
sections.html:
Start online. The assessors' real property page lists three steps: search for your parcel on qPublic, click the appeal to Board of Assessors button, and submit the form. The notice itself gives the response deadline. Georgia sets the appeal window at 45 days from the notice date.

Grounds for appeal are value, taxability, uniformity and denial of an exemption. A complaint that taxes are too high is a millage matter and cannot be appealed this way.

  • Bring photos and sale prices of similar homes nearby that sold recently.
  • Choose the board or arbitration route in your first filing.
  • After a Board of Equalization or Superior Court decision, the assessors cannot change that value for two more years without an on-site inspection.

sections.h2: What are the Rockdale County homestead exemption rules?
sections.html:
The deadline to apply is April 1 of each year, and the county says the law gives the assessors no room to extend it. Owners must live in the home and own it on January 1.

The 2026 exemption sheet lists the regular homestead as a full state exemption plus 15,000 off county maintenance and operations and 15,000 off school maintenance and operations. Other lines cover seniors, permanent disability, disabled veterans at 126,526, and income-based variable exemptions with a household income cap of $30,000. The sheet also lists a floating statewide exemption. The county HOST exemption is limited to five acres and the primary residence, and the state exemption to ten acres.

Bring a current driver's license, the recorded deed and a current utility statement to the assessors' office. Income-driven exemptions need the current federal and state tax returns. Only one homestead is allowed for each family unit.

sections.h2: When are Rockdale County property taxes due?
sections.html:
November 15 is the due date. The Tax Commissioner's tax sale page says unpaid taxes remaining after that date are subject to levy and tax sale.

Payments go in by mail with the pink return envelope, in the drop box to the right of the front door, at the window, or through an online account. Card payments carry a 2.35 percent fee with a $1.00 minimum, and the office does not take counter checks, third-party checks or payroll checks. A returned check costs at least $35 or 6 percent.

A real estate return that must be filed during the January 1 to April 1 window, for example after new construction, carries a 10 percent non-return penalty if it is late.

sections.h2: What happens in a Rockdale County tax sale?
sections.html:
Tax sales run as public auctions at the J.P. Carr Community Center in Conyers, starting at 10 a.m. The office lists March 2027 as the next sale, and the list is published in the Rockdale Citizen legal ads for four weeks beforehand. The bidder buys a tax deed, not a lien, and pays in cash or by certified check.

  • The opening bid is the tax due plus penalties and costs.
  • The buyer cannot take possession, evict tenants or improve the property right away.
  • The owner or anyone with an interest may redeem the deed, and the buyer waits one year and one day before starting a foreclosure of that right.
  • Any excess after costs may go to superior court through an interpleader action.

The Tax Commissioner's real estate resources page posts the tax sale list, an excess funds list and a delinquent tax file for download, so you can see whether a parcel is on any of them. An owner who sells before the sale pays the delinquent amount at closing. Ask the Tax Commissioner for a payoff figure before accepting any offer.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Rockdale County house with tax due?
sections.html:
Yes. The balance is settled from the sale proceeds at closing, so the buyer receives a clear title and you receive the remainder. A buyer who pays cash can remove the repair, appraisal and lender timing that slow a normal sale.

If you inherited the house, own it with tenants or are behind on payments, request a payoff from the Tax Commissioner and a value opinion from a local agent, then compare each against a cash offer.

faqs.q: What day are Rockdale County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The due date is November 15. Unpaid taxes after that date can be levied and sold at a tax sale, per the Tax Commissioner's office.

faqs.q: When must I apply for homestead exemption in Rockdale County?
faqs.a: April 1 of the tax year is the deadline, and the county says the law allows no grace period. Call the Board of Assessors at 770-278-7676 for the application, and mail goes to P.O. Box 562, Conyers, GA 30012.

faqs.q: Who decides my Rockdale County property value?
faqs.a: The Board of Assessors does, with the Chief Appraiser managing the work. Commissioners appoint the assessors and keep control only of the budget.

faqs.q: Does Rockdale County sell tax liens at auction?
faqs.a: No. The Tax Commissioner sells tax deeds only, and the office says it does not sell tax liens. The owner keeps the right to redeem.

faqs.q: What is the Rockdale County assessment ratio?
faqs.a: Property is assessed at 40 percent of market value, a rate set by Georgia law. Exemptions come off that figure before the millage rate is applied.
